M/S. Yatri Bhojan Private Limited vs State Of Odisha on 20 
December, 2024 
Author: B. P. Routray Bench: B. P. Routray Signature Not Verified Digitally Signed Signed by: MANAS KUMAR PANDA Reason: Authentication Location: OHC, Cuttack Date: 23-Dec-2024 16:15:04  IN THE HIGH COURT OF ORISSA AT CUTTACK  WP(C) No.27105 of 2024  M/s. Yatri Bhojan Private Limited,
 represented through its Managing  Director Ashish Kumar Samal .... Petitioner  Ms. D. Mohapatra, Advocate  -versus-  State of Odisha, represented through its  Principal Secretary, Home Department  and Another .... Opposite Parties  Mr. G. Tripathy, Additional Government Advocate with  Mr. D. Mohanty, Additional Government Advocate  CORAM:
 JUSTICE B. P. ROUTRAY  ORDER 20.12.2024 Order No.
03. 1. The matter is taken up through hybrid mode. 
2. Heard Ms. D. Mohapatra, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. G. Tripathy, learned AGA assisted by Mr. D. Mohanty, learned AGA. 
3. The impugned order dated 22nd October 2024 at Annexure- 13, cancelling license of the Petitioner, is subject matter of challenge before this court. 
4. Previously the Petitioner had approached this court in WP(C) No.24195 of 2024 challenging the show cause notice dated 25th September 2024 (Annexure-9) issued to it, and this court vide order dated 1st October, 2024 disposed of said writ petition stating the same as premature and with liberty to the Petitioner to challenge the final order, if any. 
M/S. Yatri Bhojan Private Limited vs State Of Odisha on 20 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71689878/ 
1 5. It is submitted on behalf of the Petitioner that this impugned order under Annexure-13 has been passed without granting any opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner on certain points which is not covered in the show cause notice under Annexure-9. To substantiate the point, it is submitted that the impugned order of cancellation of license has been passed on the premise that the Petitioner failed to maintain minimum standard of hygiene and safety in preparation of food and storage of the same, which was not a part of the show cause notice dated 19th September, 2024. 
6. Upon hearing both parties and having thorough perusal of the show cause notice under Annexure-9 and the impugned order under Annexure-13, it reveals that the language used in the show cause notice is for violation of terms of contract and the impugned order also states about violation of the terms of contract in addition to failure on the part of the Petitioner to pay license fee in time and such negligence on the part of the Petitioner relating to maintenance of minimum standard of hygiene and food safety. So, what is submitted by Ms. Mohapatra that the impugned order is beyond the scope of show cause notice served on him as per Annexure-9, is found incorrect on record. The impugned order itself reveals the opportunity of hearing granted to the Petitioner and participation of the Petitioner in the proceeding to submit his explanation. As such, no merit is seen in the contention of the Petitioner to entertain the prayer. 
7. In the result the writ petition is dismissed. 
( B.P. Routray) Judge M.K. Panda M/S. Yatri Bhojan Private Limited vs State Of Odisha on 20 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71689878/
